Damaged was the return reason with the largest returned amount for returns dated 1 to 4 October 2026, at 12.50 EUR of 24.75 EUR across 3 returns. The semantic layer has no share-of-amount metric by reason, so I cannot give that share. Fresh: returns.silver is ready up to 2026-10-03T00:00Z.

The semantic layer has no metric for days between order date and return date, so I cannot give that average. The closest metrics are Returns by order date (returns_on_order_date) and Returns (EUR), which count returns and amounts, not days.

The semantic layer has no session-duration metric, so I cannot give a median session length in minutes. The closest metric is Site sessions (site_sessions), which counts sessions with a page view by day, not their duration.

The semantic layer has no page-view-per-hour metric and no hour time grain, so I cannot give the peak hour or its count. The closest metric is site_sessions (site sessions with a page view), which is counted per day only.

The semantic layer has no median reply-time metric. The closest metrics are messages_replied (outreach messages that got a reply, by the day sent) and reply_rate (the share of messages that got a reply), and neither measures time to reply.

The semantic layer has no metric for the share of applicants who reached interview or beyond. The closest metrics are applications (candidates who applied, by the day they applied) and candidates_in_stage (candidates in each hiring stage at the end of each day), and neither gives that share.

The semantic layer has no median days-to-hire metric. The closest is time_to_hire_days (Time to hire, days), which is an average of days from applying to being hired, so it does not answer the median question.
The semantic layer has no weather or temperature metric, so I cannot compare Istanbul with Amsterdam for 1 and 2 October 2026. None of its metrics covers daily temperature.

The semantic layer has no ad-spend-per-order metric. The closest metrics are ad_spend_eur (ad spend in EUR, by day) and orders_total (all orders placed, cancelled included), and it does not divide one by the other.

The semantic layer has no calls-per-100-shipped-orders metric. The closest are calls_labelled (calls labelled by topic, a model-derived label, where delivery is a topic) and orders_total filtered to the shipped status, and no rate combines them.

The semantic layer has no median order value metric; median_order_value_eur is listed as not available in this dialect. The closest is average_order_value_eur (the average amount of a non-cancelled order), which is not a median.
The semantic layer has no 90th-percentile order metric. The closest are average_order_value_eur and revenue_eur (the sum of non-cancelled order amounts), and neither is a percentile.

The semantic layer has no metric that counts customers by number of orders above three. The closest is repeat_customers, which counts customers with a non-cancelled order in the period who have placed two or more orders in all, a different threshold.

The semantic layer has no median days-to-first-order metric. The closest is signup_to_first_order_rate, the share of customers whose first order came within 30 days of signing up, which is a rate and not a number of days.

Customers who signed up in 2024, the only pre-2026 signup year with orders in this period, averaged 102.67 EUR per non-cancelled order, against 41.00 EUR for customers who signed up in 2026, over orders placed 17 August to 10 October 2026.
